scope: Each selected mechanism has one onset per clock epoch. Groups permit a common onset time. Distinct groups require strict order.
Required responses are assumed to be observable at least once within the replay for the represented sustained episodes.
Response delays are nonnegative. A finite maximum is used only when declared for a required path and the first response has a covered normal reference.
Each first observed effect needs at least one eligible upstream path. Overlapping paths can mask a later mechanism.
Release times, repeated onsets, physical common origin and probabilities are outside the fitted model.
model_assumptions: Predictions apply to the supplied selected incident/epoch, not all aircraft systems or unobserved prehistory.
Within this finite catalogue, an effect unreachable from a candidate's roots is not explained by that candidate; a usable contrary observation rejects it.
Required effect absence is evaluated as observed absence in the current feature scope; candidates are reevaluated as evidence evolves, not permanently eliminated.
Conditional edges allow both retained and degraded downstream output; missing measurements never count as contradiction.
Detector thresholds belong to the reused evidence layer, not this hypothesis model; no native depletion rates or fixed delays are fitted here.

Propulsion predictions cover a sustained Engine 2 cutoff-like response in the pinned FlightGear study. Windmilling, partial thrust loss and additional Yellow supply mechanisms may yield other effects.
All subsets of the five selected mechanism classes are considered. Minimal compatible sets explain the observed facts without an extra root. Additional compatible roots may be masked.
A root set can fit more than one initiating history. Observation timing can constrain separate paths without identifying every command order or physical shared cause.
